forcing them to accept services in class 'D' posts for only a few years, forgoing their legitimate 
claims for 23 years. It is also noteworthy to point out that poor people travelling on trains are 
being forced to change the food habits from hot puri-sabji or roti-sabji to burgers and 
sandwiches.  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. VELU): 
We have not done this. It is just an option given.  
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: Okay, you make it clear i n your reply, yesterday, 
while discussing on the subject of rural development, a request was made for allowing the 
Self-Help Groups to sell their products on the railway stations.  
The hon. Rural Development Minister said that he would be taking up this matter with 
the hon. Railway Minister as to why the Self-Help G roups were not allowed to sell their 
products at all the Railway stations.  
Sir, the hon. Railway Minister announced that licensed coolies would be given jobs in the 
Railways. It is a very good announcement. Sir, may I ask the hon. Minister to give a time-
frame for this noble project? I would like to know from the hon. Minister as to how many 
coolies are having valid licenses, and how many of them are fit for appointment. Have you 
started assessing the situation? What is the time-frame? This is a very noble project which 
has been announced by the Railway Minister.  
Sir, the posts of Gangmen are Class 'D' posts, and the Sixth Pay Commission has suggested 
that no further recruitment to Class "D" posts woul d be done. This is another picture. As 
such, I am afraid, this announcement may turn to be a mirage.  
A few years ago, the hon. Railways Minister, Shri Lalu ji, in one of his finest speeches in 
Kolkata declared that railway hawkers would be give n licences. But, on the contrary, the 
poor railway hawkers are being thrown out of their jobs, which is the only source of their 
income. So far, none of them has been bessed with a licence.  
In the recent past, the Railway has decided to clos e down the Railway Printing Presses 
and outsource the printing jobs. The argument of th e Railways in favour of this plan was 
that, following computerisation of stations, there was no need to run the Printing Presses. 
This is ridiculous. There are not only around 7000 'E' and 'F' categories of stations, where 
printed tickets are still required, but, a large number of forms and other official materials are 
also required to be printed by these Railway Presses.  
Sir I think, the hon. Railway Minister will mention  in his reply about conversion of 
metre-gauge into broad guage in the North Eastern part of the country.  
Sir, it is praiseworthy that reduction in Railway fares is taking place But, Sir, the plight 
of the Railway daily passengers in the suburban tra ins, lack of amenities in long distance 
trains, and safety and security of the commuters are matters of major concerns for all of us.

There are reports that many a times; reserved passengers do not get berths due to 
unauthorised occupation by non-ticket travellers. This is another point which I wanted to 
make. 
Lastly, Sir, I would like to point out here that in Delhi, underground metro is being 
connected with the Airport. It is connected with the Railway Station also. This is a very 
welcome step. But, Sir, in Kolkata, which is a very congested metropolis, that was not done. 
Recently, an elevated circular rail was extended from Dum-Dum Station up to the Airport, 
completely disregarding the request for extension of underground metro. There will be no 
passengers in the circular rail. Who will go in the circular rail? It will take a very long time 
for the passengers going to the Airport. So, what has happended now? The Railway 
Administration admits this. The hon. Railway Minister had given me a reply that there were 
no passengers. So, I demand of the Railway Administration to extend underground metro 
services up to the Kolkata Airport. The West Bengal Goverment has initiated a programme 
to connect the underground metro with the Railway Stations at Sialdah and Howrah. Kolkata 
is the most congested city of this country. With these words, I support the Appropriation 
(Railways) No. 3 Bill, 2008. Thank you, Sir.

SHRI RAMA CHANDRA KHUNTIA (Orissa): Sir, I, on behalf of the Indian National 
Congress, support the Appropriation (Railways) No. 3 Bill which is being discussed today. 
As we all know, the railway activities in our country and the Budget placed by our Railway 
Minister are not only supported by the UPA Government, but has also been appreciated and 
got the appreciation from all corners. If you go into the details of the Budget, you will find 
something which we have not seen before. The gross traffic revenue is at Rs. 72,755 crore, 
that is, 16 point higher and the return of the capi tal is 21 per cent. The cash surplus before 
dividend is expected to be Rs. 25,000 crore in 2008 , and by the year end is likely be Rs. 
20,483 crore, that is, 27 per cent more than the Budget target. The Railways from all sides 
is being appreciated. If we go into the details, the main thing of the Railways is the railway 
safety. The number of accidents has been reduced. The number of persons killed in railway 
accidents has also been reduced. The train accident s due to collision have been reduced 
from 130 in 2005-06 to 95, and the total accident cases have been reduced from 233 to 194. 
Passengers killed in 2005-06 were 168, which have b een reduced to 38; injuries in 2005 
have been reduced from 483 to 227 and the cases of persons killed in 2005-06 have been 
reduced from 9 to 6 in 2006-07. So, there are two things. One is, Budget expenditure, profit 
and appreciation and second is the concessions give n to the general public. Within this 
period of the UPA Government and in the Budget plac ed by the very renowned and 
famous Minister, Lalu Prasadji, there is no increase in the passenger fares and, on the other 
hand, concessions have been given to senior citizens, women, AIDS-affected persons, students 
and to the families of those persons who are killed in the defence action. The concession has 
also been given to those who are needy. So, from al l sides, the Railway Budget and the 
railway activities in our country are very much appreciated. I congratulate the Railway Minister 
for his performance in the country. While saying so, Sir. I will add one or two suggestions 
about the Railway safety. I would like to know from the hon. Railway Minister: What is the

total number of old railway tracks and bridges in the country which have already been declared 
unsafe, and how much time will it take to replace these old railway tracks and also to complete 
these bridges which have been declared unsafe and are not in good conditions? It is one of 
the most important points for the railway safety. S econdly, some people have mentioned 
about the railway stations. Till now also, many peo ple are entering the railway sites and 
occupying the seats in the first and second-class waiting rooms. In the night time also many 
people without tickets sleep inside the railway stations which is also becoming the cause of 
threat and many types of violence. What steps will the hon. Minister take to prevent this so 
that these things do not happen inside the railway stations? In addition to that, I think, one 
hon. Member asked here and I would also like to ask  as to what is the criterion for the 
allocation of funds in the Railway Budget which are given to different States. It is also a fact 
that many States in our country have got the longer railway lines. I do not want to name those 
States. But, at the same time, there are many States, including Jammu and Kashmir, North-
Eastern States and my State, Orissa, which have got the shorter railway lines in comparison 
to other States. So, while allocating funds for new  railway lines, the fact that States with 
shorter railway routes need more emphasis should be kept in mind. I want to say that those 
States, which have shorter railway lines, should also be given equal importance.  
Then, hon. Railway Minister has done a very good thing. He has allocated the money in 
view of the Pay Commission's Report. If they have t o pay more for the employees and 
officers, they have made a provision for that in the Railway Budget. I think, that is a good 
thing.  
Regarding regularisation of coolies, I would like to say that hon. Minister has done a very 
good job by regularising the coolies who have been passing their days in a very distressed 
condition for a long time. It is a historic decision that the hon. Railway Minister has taken to 
regularise them. It will be a very good thing if they get their jobs.  
Then, I would like to mention about the people who are living on the railway land. There 
are many such people in Bilaspur and Raipur in Chha ttisgarh. They are living on railway 
land in Rourkela, Berhampur, Sambalpur and Cuttack in Orissa. In West Bengal also, they 
are living in Kharagpur, Howrah, and at many other stations. So, just telling them that they 
cannot occupy this land and just throwing them out because this is railway land is not a 
humane decision. We have also to consider that these people have been living there for 30-
40 years. Now, without making any alternative arran gement, if we just throw them out, I 
think, the hon. Railway Minister being a leader of the poor people, should consider their 
condition. I have also given a representation. I hope, the hon. Minister will consider it and 
before eviction of these people, some alternative a rrangement or a small place can be 
earmarked where multistoreyed flats can be construc ted and sold to these people. Such a 
step can be taken in consultation with the State Governments.  
SHRI R. VELU: Sir, 1 would like to make it clear that housing is the responsibility of the 
State Governments. The Supreme Court has said that railway land cannot be allotted for 
housing purpose. That being the case, you should go  back to the States and ask them to 
provide alternative sites. Till then, we are also evicting them in a systematic way. What I am 
trying to say is that we are sympathetic towards these people, but we cannot allow the railway 
land to be encroached upon.  
SHRI RAMA CHANDRA KHUNTIA: I think, the Railway Ministry can have negotiation 
with the State Governments. We are also asking the State Governments to provide some alternative 
site for their rehabilitation. If that can be done, I think, it will be useful for these people.

Then, about employment, a statement came in an Oriya newspaper that the Oriya people 
are not getting employment because they are not well trained and their skill level is not as 
per the requirement. My appeal to the hon. Minister is that as the Railways are using the 
services of 15 lakhs people in the country and being such a big organisation, the Railway 
Ministry can also start some centres to give training to the workers to upgrade their skills so 
that these can be useful for the railways. Those who are working at lower levels can go to 
higher levels. Is the Railway Ministry considering any such training programme for skill 
upgradation of its employees. Sir, I belong to Orissa, and, I have some suggestions to 
make in this context. Sir, I am thankful to the Railway Minister for making a good allocation 
in the Railway Budget for the State of Orissa in comparison to previous years. But, as I 
have already said, we have many projects pending in the State of Orissa and the Railway is 
also having some surplus revenue. Sir, as many industries are coming up in Orissa, I 
request the Railway Minister to consider giving some more amount to it so that these 
projects can be completed. Khurda-Bolangir railway line, Koraput-Gunupur, Jakhapura-
Bansapani Railway doubling line, Haridaspur-Paradip Railway Line, Talcher-Paradip 
doubling line, completion of Bangirposi broad gauge work, etc. and all other Railway 
projects which are pending in the State of Orissa should be taken up. There is also a 
proposal for the survey of a new railway line from Jajpur-Keonjhar Road to Dhamra Port 
in Orissa via Navi Gaya i.e. Baitarankhetra-Jajpur-Akhandalmani so that this can connect 
two holy places and tourist places also, and, also there can be a direct railway connection till 
Dharma Port for transporting minerals. In this way, the pressure on Paradip Port is lessened 
and this can directly connect the Dharma Port of Orissa. 
Sir, another railway line is required from Berhampur to Miniguda via Phulbani and 
Jiudaigiri so that these two tribal Districts - where there is no railway line — can be connected. 
Sir, this is also an important thing. Sir, I know that the East Coast Zone has been declared, 
but the office of the General Manager and other offices, I think, are in the process of 
construction. I would also like to mention that the Jajpur-Keonjhar Road is an important 
railway line. Sir, many steel industries like Jindal, Tata and Neelanchal Ispat Nigam Limited, 
etc. are coming up there. This is also connected with Bansapani, Sukinda mines areas and 
the Paradip Port. So, I would like to know whether the Railway Minister would consider 
having the office of Divisional Manager at Jajpur Road so that it becomes easy for 
transportation of goods in this area. 
With these words, I, once again, support the Railway Appropriation Bill. Sir, if you see 
the performance of Railway during the UPA Government, it is far better than that of the 
NDA Government from any angle, i.e., number of accidents, safety, revenue receipts, profits, 
etc., and this year's Railway Budget is definitely good. So, on behalf of the Congress 
Party, I suport the Railway Appropriation Bill and congratulate the Railway Minister for 
presenting this Budget.

DR. BIMAL JALAN (Nominated): Sir, I thank you for giving me the opportunity to 
speak. Sir, as required and suggested by you, I shall be very, very brief, and, just emphasise 
on a few important points. One, Sir, is the great economic importance of an efficient railway 
system for us. We have had Railways for a very, very long time, more than a century, so we 
take if for granted. But an efficient railway system, to my mind, is an absolutely essential 
input to high economic growth. Because transport of all raw materials, all capital goods and 
machinery is dependent on a efficient railway system. In the present circumstances, if you 
want high growth rate, or, if you want rural development, or, if you want any sector of our 
economy to develop, I would suggest that we should provide maximum support, financial 
support, to the Railways. 
The second point that I want to make is in regard to the example which the hon. Railway 
Minister has set for the rest of the public sector. If there is a will, if there is an effort, if there 
is an authority, and if there is an organisation, then our public sector can be efficient, can 
support itself, and can provide the kind of services that the rest of India needs. This is the 
second point which I want to make. 
We have to learn a lot from what has happened in the railway system, to bring us to a 
point, where it is providing resources, where we don't have to raise freights, and where we 
don't have to raise passenger fares to be able to generate resources. This is the efficient use 
of whatever material you have both human as well as financial services and the present 
Railway Minister has been able to provide that. I think that this is a great example for the rest 
of the public sector that it can be done, if you have the will. Thank you, Sir. 
SHRI PYARIMOHAN MOHAPATRA (Orissa): Sir, I thank the hon. Railway Minister 
for presenting a good budget. The Railway Minister has been quite competent in tackling the 
Railways, as my colleague, Dr. Jalan, pointed out. The Railway infrastructure is the most 
important one, among all means of transport, to ensure economic growth. I wish the entire 
country had been the focus and not some areas because of one's likes or because of certain 
pressures whether political or economical. 
Have a Backward Region Fund. We, in Orissa and in a number of other States like Jammu 
and Kashmir and the North-Eastern States, are well below half the national average. We 
don't say that you take us to the national average of railway kilometerage within a span of 
five years. We say that you take us up to that level within a span of ten years. You have to 
have the will. Why not create a Backward Region Railway Fund? Bihar was lucky in having 
successive Railway Ministers. Viability is not a criterion when you go for expansion of 
railway network in Bihar. We are continuously being told about the viability of Khurda-
Bolangir railway line which is the lifeline of Orissa. It opens up backward regions of Orissa. 
My friend, Shri Khuntia, pointed out a number of railway lines. I will add a few more. 
Take Gopalpur-Rayagada railway line, going through the backward region. It does not have 
any infrastructure at all. Take Jajpur-Malkangiri, Gunupur-Bissamcuttack, and Talcher-
Bimlagarh railway lines. I just like to draw the attention of the Minister towards this. Talcher 
this year has produced 70 million tonnes of coal. It is a useless station. It is going to produce, 
in seven years, 200 million tonnes of coal, a lot of which will go down to the South. What are 
you doing about it? You talk of world class station for Bhubaneshwar. Why not world class 
stations for Talcher, Jharsaguda, Jajpur-Keonjhar road and Raigada, four places in Orissa, 
which are industrial and mining hubs? It is a pity that thinking is not going into this. Kindly 
remember that poverty, as Dr. Jalan said, cannot be really effectively tackled unless you 
have a good railway infrastructure. (Time Bell). I will take a couple of minutes. When

Shri R. Velu was there in Bhubaneshwar, I mentioned about what the requirement is if you 
want to bring Orissa on to half of the national ave rage of railway kilometreage iri 5 years' 
time, put Rs. 2000 crores a year, to finish the on-going projects, to carry on with your normal 
electrification, doubling, all these kinds of work, and also to start some new projects which 
can go over to the Twelfth Plan.

SHRI PYARIMOHAN MOHAPATRA: I am not going to the detailed suggestions one by 
one. I merely mentioned the suggestions relating to bringing Orissa on to half of the national 
average of railway kilometreage in 5 years' time, w hat the requirement is. Secondly, on 
general issues, inspite of the excellent performance of the Railways, on general issues, inspite 
of the excellent performance of the Railways, I will point out three issues which need to be 
looked after. One is, track maintenance. Your performance may be excellent in all respects, 
track maintenance would be average. Passengers amenities, again, they are between average 
and good. Quality of service in coaches, again average. I don't call them bad, again average. 
Kindly improve these so that your performance in all aspects becomes excellent. If anybody 
says that you are charging too much in terms of passenger fares,,I would say, no, you are one

THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH): Shri Siva, Now; brevity is 
the soul of wit. 
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (Tamil Nadu): Thank you, Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, I rise to sup-
port the Appropriation (Railways), No. 3 Bill, 2008. The railways, an effective mode of 
transport for long distance travel and movement of goods, have seen a steady rise in the cash 
surplus from Rs. 9,000 crores in the year 2005 to Rs. 14,000 crores in 2006, Rs. 20,000 
crores in 2007 and Rs. 25,000 crores in the year 2008, that too after Laluji has assumed 
power. 
While appreciating the Minister, I would like to know from him as to why there is a 
declaration in acquisition of wagons. In the year 1990-91, the number of wagons in the 
railways was 3.5 lakhs. In 2005-06, it was only 2 lakhs. In 15 years, there is a sharp decline 
of 1 lakh wagons! While the railways have not achieved the target in the past years, it has 
fixed a target of 10,000 wagons to be acquired in the current year. I do not know how it 
would be possible. 
Coming to the next point, the fares have been reduced very much and the people prefer 
the transport of railways better than the road transport for safety, comfort and for cheaper 

180   Government  [RAJYA SABHA]  Bills  
mode of travel. When more and more people are seeking the railways transport, the railways 
are maintaining the same route and the same number of coaches. So, the essentiality of 
doubling the lines becomes a must. 1 would like to bring to the notice of the Minister that 
while doubling the Villupuram and Dindigul line, he should also consider doubling Tiruchi-
Tanjavur, the vital line. Adequate space is available after the meter-gauge is converted into 
broad-gauge.  
Before that doubling, I would like suggest to the Minister that a shuttle train could be run 
between Trichy and Thanjavur because every second minute a bus plies from Trichy to 
Thanjavur. This train if it could be a demu-rake, I think, that itself would suffice the needs of 
the people there and the patronage will be very much and the revenue will also grow up. So, 
1 would also like to request for expediting the proposal which has been given in the Budget 
for Karaikudi-Tutukudi conversion line. To proposal, which I had made in my earlier speech 
about Trichy-Tirunelveli Intercity Express and day train from Trichy to Bangalore via Ariyalur-
Viruddhachalam and Salem, could also be brought. An interaction with MPs could help a 
lot. Passenger amenities have been increased but I have to mention here that many of the 
things have not come to the knowledge of the local MPs. The officials themselves launch 
without bringing them to the Knowledge of the MPs. This is creating distance between the 
people and their representatives because these amenities are being launched without inform-
ing the representatives of the people. Sir, one more thing is that the Railways employ 1.5 
million employees, and taking care of all of them is a must. Almost all the Railway hospitals 
have a dearth of Specialist Doctors. The Specialist Doctors are attending the employees who 
are ill only on request. I with Laluji who has brought a very good success to the Railways 
will realize the welfare of the employees who form the base of this success and the hospitals 
should be given more Specialist Doctors. With these words, I support the Bill and hope my 
observations will receive positive response from the Minister. Thank you.  
SHRI SANJAY RAUT (Maharashtra): Sir, I thank you very much for giving me this 
opportunity to speak on the Appropriation (Railways) No. 3 Bill, 2008. Sir, it is a great 
pleasure for all of us that the Indian Railways, the world's biggest rail service provider, have 
been making a good profit. Needless to say here, the Indian Railways have always stood as 
the backbone of India's economy. Sir, as all of us know that Mumbai is better known as the 
financial capital of India and, therefore, it is necessary that all railway projects for Maharashtra 
State pending with the Railway Ministry are given priority and completed in a time-bound 
phase. To my knowledge, there are several railway projects, to name a few, the new railway 
line, widening of existing railway lines, doubling of existing railway lines, etc., which are 
yet to be completed. Sir, another project regarding extension and modernization of Chatrapati 
Shivaji Terminus, which has been given recognition by UNESCO as one of the world's 
heritage site, is awaiting approval of the Railway Board. Maharashtra Government has pointed 
out that 20 acres of land exists near the CST Railway Station, which may be developed for a 
new terminal on BoT basis. Sir, through you, I would like to request the hon. Minister of 
Railways to ensure its early completion. A proposal of Maharashtra Government for the 
attachment of Nanded Railway Division to Central Railway has not been found feasible by 
the Railway Ministry. I would like to request the hon. Minister to get the matter re-examined 
in the light of utilities attached to it. The hon. Railway Minister in his budget speech in-
formed the House about the target of completion of gauge conversion of about 2150 kilometres 
during 2008-2009, including some sections in Maharashtra, namely, Miraj-Lattur, 374 kms., 
and Solapur Hotgi Gadag, 284 kms. But no specific time limit has been fixed for their  

Government  [22 APRIL 2008]  Bills   181  
completion. I, therefore, request the hon. Minister to fix a time-bound programme for comple-
tion of these projects. Sir, as the House is aware the suburban services are the lifeline of 
Mumbai. The existing suburban services are not able to cope with the huge rush and there-
fore needs some more locals for Mumbaikars.  
[THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN) in the Chair.]  
To my knowledge, the Railways have not been able to acquire the sufficient number of 
additional local trains so far, to which the railway should accord priority. The Railway Min-
ister in his budget speech has pointed out that even after the completion of MUTP Phase-I, 
which is being undertaken with the assistance of the World Bank and Phase-II, the suburban 
services will not be able to meet the demand of the ever-increasing population.  
Hon. Minister has himself realised that there is a perceived need to introduce AC train 
services in Mumbai for which Railways have decided to conduct a pre-feasibility study for 
introduction of an elevated fully air-conditioned Metro Service between Mumbai Central 
and Virar Station on Western Railway.  
Now, through you, Sir, I would like to know from the hon. Railway Minister whether he 
intends to get a pre-feasibility study for AC Metro Service done for the benefit of Mumbaikars 
on a top priority basis.  
Sir, before I conclude, I demand that additional locals, which is the backbone of the daily 
commuters, should be acquired by the Railways on a priority basis so that the Mumbaikars 
are benefited. I would also like that the hon. Railway Minister should assure the House chat 
whatever be the proposals already pending for the last more than 6-10 years, as also new 
proposals received from the Maharashtra Government, will be completed at the earliest.  
SHRI BIRENDRAPRASAD BAISHYA (Assam): Respected Vice-Chairman, Sir, I am 
really thankful to you for giving me this opportunity to speak on the Appropriation (Railways) 
No. 3 Bill. Sir, I would like to congratulate the hon. Railway Minister, Shri Lalu Prasad 
Yadavji for giving us i surplus Budget, but, at the same time, I would like  to draw the 
attention of the hon. Mnister regarding few important issues of Railways in the State of 
Assam and North-Eastern Regions. Sir, in your Budge t Speech, an additional fund of 
Rs. 1712 crores was sought from the Ministry of Finance for National projects like Bogibeel 
Rail cum Road Bridge, Lunding-Silchar-Jiribum, Rangiya-Murkongseleck gauge conversion 
and others declared National projects. But, it did not reflect anywhere in the General Budget 
announced by the hon. Finance Minister. We believe that you will clear those National 
projects through Supplementary Budget to expedite gauge conversion works, ensuring its 
completion in a time frame, which is delayed mostly due to lack of funds, to improve the 
existing services of meter gauge sections including replacement of outdated coaches with 
new coaches, improvement of servicing and regular maintenance of MG coaches and to look 
at the present deplorable conditions due to obious negligence in anticipation of BG 
conversion. Sir, replacement of irrepairable coached running without minimum hygienic 
conditions of toilet facilities including water supply and lighting, needs to be reviewed 
urgently. The people of Assam were demanding a coach factory for several years. So, I 
would request the hon. Minister to kindly set up a coach factory in Assam. Sir, I would 
request the gauge conversion of the remaining few kilometres, Dangori-laikhowa part of 
Tinsukia Division of NF Railway in Assam which was left out from Dibru-Saikhowa line 20 
years back under uni-gauge programme of the Ministry be completed. A survey for this route 
was completed in November 2008. Execution of this small portion of gauge conversion will 
greatly contribute towards  

182   Government [RAJYASABHA] Bills 
gaining a positive rate of return in the near future since it is linked to a very commercially 
viable terminal at Dhola-Saikhowa. Hope this project will be included in the Budget with 
your kind intervention. 
Sir, unemployment is a very big problem in Assam. Local youth is totally deprived of 
Railway jobs for many years. Therefore, employment to local youth in the 3rd and 4th grade 
posts will be helpful in minimising the unemployment problem as well as, to some extent, 
insurgency in the State. So, I would like to request the hon. Railway Minister to 100% Job 
reserve 3rd and 4th grade posts for the local unemployed youth. In Assam. This is very 
important. Sir, unemployment is a very big broblem in my State. If you provide employment, 
it brings down insurgency. So, in the interest of the national integrity, in the interest of the 
nation, I would like to request the hon. Railway Minister to kindly 100% Job reservation on 
3rd and 4th grade post local youth in Assam. Thank you.
